# Introduction

A key measure of a country's integration into the global economy is **trade openness**, calculated as the sum of exports and imports divided by GDP (expressed as a percentage).
A central question in understanding globalization is whether more open economies tend to be richer.
The examination of this question is the primary subject of this exam.

The exam has three parts with a sum of **30 points**:

1.  Loading and wrangling data (10 points)

2.  Describing and visualizing data (10 points)

3.  Fitting a model to data (10 points)
